description:
A SWML document for handling inbound and outbound calls. Contains a `sections` map where
each section holds an array of methods that run sequentially. Execution starts at
`sections.main`. See the [Calling SWML reference](/docs/swml/reference/calling) for the
full list of available methods.
title: Calling SWML Document

max_duration.description: Maximum duration in seconds for the call. Defaults to `14400` seconds (4 hours).

codecs.description:
Codecs to offer, as a comma-separated string or an array of strings with one codec per entry.
Each array entry can also be a SWML variable reference that is resolved when the method runs.
Valid codecs depend on the call type: phone calls accept PCMU, PCMA, G722, G729 and AMR-WB;
SIP and WebRTC calls also accept OPUS, VP8 and H264.
If the codecs are not valid for the call type, they are ignored, a `relay_script_method_parameter_invalid_value`
warning is reported, and `answer` continues without them.

username.description:
Username to use for SIP authentication challenges.
Applied only together with a `password` that is not empty after variable expansion.

password.description:
Password to use for SIP authentication challenges.
When it is not empty after variable expansion, it is applied together with `username`.

answer.description: Answer incoming call and set an optional maximum duration.
answer.title: answer

ai.description:
Creates an AI agent that conducts voice conversations using automatic speech recognition (ASR),
large language models (LLMs), and text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis.
The agent processes caller speech in real-time, generates contextually appropriate responses,
and can execute custom functions to interact with external systems through SignalWire AI Gateway (SWAIG).
ai.title: ai

ai_sidecar.description:
Attach a real-time AI observer that listens to a live call and streams agent-facing advice to your application as webhook callbacks.
The sidecar does not participate in the call; it watches the conversation and produces structured callbacks your application can consume.
With `action.summarize`, the request instead summarizes the conversation using the sidecar already attached to the call.
ai_sidecar.title: ai_sidecar

amazon_bedrock.description: Creates a new Bedrock AI Agent

cond.description:
Execute a sequence of instructions depending on the value of a JavaScript condition.
Conditions are checked in array order. The first condition whose `when` evaluates to true runs its `then` instructions,
and the remaining conditions are skipped. The `else` entry runs only when no condition evaluates to true.
At most one `else` entry is allowed, and it doesn't have to be the last entry.
When no condition matches and there is no `else` entry, execution continues with the next method after `cond`.
cond.title: cond

connect.description: Connect to a phone number, SIP URI, Resource Address, queue, or WebSocket stream.

denoise.description:
Start noise reduction.
For an inbound call that has not been answered and is not ending, the method attempts to answer it before starting noise reduction.
You can stop it at any time using `stop_denoise`.

enter_queue.description:
Place the current call in a named queue where it will wait to be connected to an available agent or resource.
While waiting, callers will hear music or custom audio.
When an agent connects to the queue (using the connect method), the caller and agent are bridged together.
After the bridge completes, execution continues with the SWML script specified in execute_after_queue,
or the call hangs up if none was given.
enter_queue.title: enter_queue

dest.description:
Specifies what to execute. The value can be one of:
- `<section_name>` - section in the current document to execute
- A URL (http or https) that returns a SWML document - Sends HTTP POST
- An inline SWML document (as a JSON string)

params.description:
Named parameters to send to section or URL.
After variable expansion, `params` can nest objects and arrays at most 63 levels deep, counting the `params` object itself.
If `params` is nested deeper, the section or URL is not executed, a `relay_script_nested_too_deep` warning is reported,
and the methods after `execute` in the current section don't run.

on_return.description: The list of SWML instructions to be executed when the executed section or URL returns

anyOf.description:
Execute a sequence of instructions depending on the value of a JavaScript condition.
Conditions are checked in array order. The first condition whose `when` evaluates to true runs its `then` instructions,
and the remaining conditions are skipped. The `else` entry runs only when no condition evaluates to true.
At most one `else` entry is allowed, and it doesn't have to be the last entry.
When no condition matches and there is no `else` entry, execution continues with the next method after `cond`.
anyOf.title: cond

result.description:
Instructions to run based on the value returned by the executed section or URL.
`result` is processed after the section or URL returns and before `on_return`, and only when the section or URL set a `return_value` (for example, with the return method).
An object-shaped `result` is handled like the switch method: its `case` keys are matched against `return_value`.
An array-shaped `result` is handled like the cond method: a list of conditions checked in order.

execute.description:
Execute a specified section or URL as a subroutine, and upon completion, return to the current document.
Use the return statement to pass any return values or objects back to the current document.

label.description:
Name of the label to jump to. It must match a label defined with the label method.
A SWML variable reference is resolved when the goto runs.

when.description: A JavaScript condition that determines whether to perform the jump. If the condition evaluates to true, the jump is executed. If omitted, the jump is unconditional.

max.description:
The maximum number of times to perform the jump. Must be a number between 1 and 100, or a SWML variable reference that resolves to one. Default `100`.
The jump count belongs to the target label: every goto in the current execution that jumps to the same label adds to that count,
and each goto compares its own `max` against it. Once the count reaches `max`, the jump is skipped and execution continues with the next method.

goto.description:
Jump to a label within the current section, optionally based on a condition.
The goto method will only navigate to a label within the same section.

label.description:
Mark any point of the SWML section with a label so that goto can jump to it.
The label name must be a nonempty string, and label names must be unique within the section.

action.description: The action to perform during live transcription.

live_transcribe.description: Start live transcription of the call. The transcription will be sent to the specified webhook URL.
live_transcribe.title: live_transcribe

action.description:
The action to perform during live translation.
Accepts a SWML variable reference that resolves to one of the supported actions.

live_translate.description: Start live translation of the call. The translation will be sent to the specified webhook URL.
live_translate.title: live_translate

reason.description:
The reason for hanging up the call: `hangup`, `cancel`, `busy`, `noAnswer`, `decline` or `error`.
Can also be a SWML variable reference that resolves to one of these values.

The reason only affects calls that are inbound and not yet answered: when omitted,
`hangup` or `busy`, the call is rejected as busy (SIP `486 Busy Here`); any other value rejects it
as declined (SIP `603 Decline`).
An answered call ends normally and an unanswered outbound call is canceled, whatever the reason.

hangup.description: End the call with an optional reason.
hangup.title: hangup

name.description:
Name of the room to join. Allowed characters: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, and hyphen.
The room name, after variable expansion, can be at most 100 characters.

join_room.description:
Join a Relay room. If the call is an unanswered inbound call, the method first tries to answer it.
If the room doesn't exist, it creates a new room. A room created this way is set to be deleted after its
room sessions end; an existing room keeps its own settings.
join_room.title: join_room

join_conference.description:
Join an ad-hoc audio conference started on either the SignalWire or Compatibility API.
This method allows you to connect the current call to a named conference where multiple participants can communicate simultaneously.
join_conference.title: join_conference

play.description: Play file(s), ringtones, speech or silence.
play.title: play

examples: say:Please press 1 for sales or 2 for support
play.description:
URL or array of URLs to play.
Each entry can be a playable URL or a SWML variable that resolves to one.
Allowed URLs are:
    http:// or https:// - audio file to GET
    ring:[duration:]<ringtone> - ring tone to play, named by country code or `bong`. For example: ring:us to play single ring or ring:20.0:us to play ring for 20 seconds. A duration, when given, must be at least 1 second.
    say:<text to speak> - Sentence to say
    silence: <duration> - seconds of silence to play, at least 1

volume.description:
Volume level for the audio file.
Default is `0`.
Valid range is -40 to 40.

say_voice.description:
The voice to use for `say:` text to speech.
When not set, the `say_voice` SWML variable is used if it is set.
Otherwise, a voice is selected based on the text-to-speech language and gender.
A voice name must not contain whitespace, double quotes, or any of the characters `,{}()[]<>=/;!@#$%^&*+|~?` or a backtick.

say_language.description:
The language to use for `say:` text to speech, as a language tag such as `en-US`.
When not set, the `say_language` SWML variable is used if it is set, otherwise `en-US`.

say_gender.description:
The gender to use for `say:` text to speech: `male` or `female`.
When not set, the `say_gender` SWML variable is used if it is set, otherwise `female`.

max_digits.description:
Number of digits to collect. Must be at least `1`. Values above `100` are capped at `100`.
Default is `1`.

terminators.description:
Digits that terminate digit collection.
Default is not set.

digit_timeout.description:
Time in seconds to wait for next digit. Must be at least `1`.
Default is `5.0` seconds.

initial_timeout.description:
Time in seconds to wait for start of input. Must be at least `1`.
Default is `5.0` seconds.

speech_timeout.description: Max time in seconds to wait for speech result. Must be at least `1`.

speech_end_timeout.description: Time in seconds to wait for end of speech utterance. Must be at least `1`.

speech_language.description:
Language to detect speech in, as a language tag such as `en-US`.
Extension and private-use subtags are not accepted.

speech_hints.description:
Expected words or phrases to help the speech recognition.
Each hint must be a non-empty string and is sent as written: SWML variables in hints are not expanded.
Hints longer than 100 bytes or containing `=` are ignored.
Hints after the first 5000, or after 100,000 bytes in total, are dropped.

speech_engine.description:
The engine that is selected for speech recognition. The engine must support the specified language.
Default is not set (SignalWire picks the engine).

status_url.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL to deliver prompt status events, or a SWML variable that resolves to one.

prompt.description:
Play a prompt and wait for input. The input can be received either as digits from the keypad,
or from speech, or both depending on what parameters are set.
By default, only digit input is enabled.
To enable speech input, set at least one of `speech_timeout`, `speech_end_timeout`, `speech_language`, or `speech_hints`.
Setting `speech_engine` alone does not enable speech input.
To enable both digit and speech input, also set at least one of `max_digits`, `terminators`, or `digit_timeout`.
`initial_timeout` controls how long to wait for input and does not select an input mode.
prompt.title: prompt

status_url.description:
http or https URL to deliver receive_fax status events.
Can also be a SWML variable reference, substituted when the method runs; the resolved value
must be an http or https URL.

receive_fax.description: Receive a fax being delivered to this call.
receive_fax.title: receive_fax

stereo.description:
If true, record in stereo.
Default is `false`.

format.description:
The format to record in. Can be `wav`, `mp3`, or `mp4`.
Default is `"wav"`.

direction.description:
Direction of the audio to record: "speak" for what party says, "listen" for what party hears, "both" for what the party hears and says.
Default is `"speak"`.

terminators.description: String of digits that will stop the recording when pressed. Default is `"#"`.

beep.description:
Play a beep when recording starts. Recording starts at the same time as the beep, so the beep can be included in the recording.
Default is `false`.

input_sensitivity.description:
How sensitive the recording voice activity detector is to background noise.
A larger value is more sensitive. Allowed values from 0.0 to 100.0.
Default is `44.0`.

initial_timeout.description:
Time in seconds to wait for the start of speech.
Default is `4.0` seconds.

end_silence_timeout.description:
Time in seconds to wait in silence before ending the recording.
Default is `5.0` seconds.

max_length.description:
Maximum length of the recording in seconds.
Default is `0`, which sets no maximum length. The recording can still end for other reasons, such as a terminator digit or a timeout.

status_url.description: URL to send recording status events to.

record.description:
Record the call audio in the foreground, pausing further SWML execution until recording ends.
Use this, for example, to record voicemails.
To record calls in the background in a non-blocking fashion, use the record_call method.
record.title: record

control_id.description:
Identifier for this recording, to use with `stop_record_call`.
When not set or empty, an identifier is generated and saved to the `record_control_id` variable.
The identifier, after variable expansion, must not contain `{`, `}`, commas, semicolons, apostrophes, backslashes, or ASCII control characters; otherwise the recording fails to start.

stereo.description:
If `true`, record in stereo.
Default is `false`.

format.description:
The format to record in. It can be `wav`, `mp3`, or `mp4`.
Default is `"wav"`.

direction.description:
Direction of the audio to record: "speak" for what party says, "listen" for what party hears, "both" for what the party hears and says.
Default is `"both"`.

terminators.description: String of digits that will stop the recording when pressed. Default is `""` (empty).

beep.description:
Play a beep when recording starts. Recording starts at the same time as the beep, so the beep can be included in the recording.
Default is `false`.

input_sensitivity.description:
How sensitive the recording voice activity detector is to background noise.
Only used when `initial_timeout` or `end_silence_timeout` is greater than `0`; with both at their default of `0`, the recording is continuous and this setting is ignored.
A larger value is more sensitive. Allowed values from 0.0 to 100.0.
Default is `44.0`.

initial_timeout.description:
Time in seconds to wait for the start of speech.
Default is `0.0` seconds.

end_silence_timeout.description:
Time in seconds to wait in silence before ending the recording.
Default is `0.0` seconds.

max_length.description:
Maximum length of the recording in seconds.
Default is `0`, which sets no maximum length. The recording can still end for other reasons, such as a terminator digit or `stop_record_call`.

status_url.description: http or https URL to deliver record_call status events

record_call.description:
Record call in the background.
Unlike the record method, the record_call method will start the recording and continue executing
the SWML script while allowing the recording to happen in the background.
To stop call recordings started with record_call, use the stop_record_call method.
record_call.title: record_call

url.description: URL to send the HTTPS request to. Authentication can also be set in the URL in the format of username:password@url.

method.description:
The HTTP method to be used for the request. Can be `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, or `DELETE`.
A SWML variable reference is also accepted; it must resolve to one of these methods.

headers.description:
Object mapping HTTP header names to string values.
Valid header names are `Accept`, `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, and `Range` (case-insensitive), and custom headers
that start with `X-` (or `x-`) followed by one or more ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores.
Header values support variable substitution. After substitution, a value must be non-empty and contain only printable
ASCII characters (spaces included) other than the backslash; tabs, line breaks, and non-ASCII characters are not allowed.
Entries with an invalid name, a non-string value, or an invalid value are skipped with a warning, and the request is
still sent.

body.description:
Request body. Content-Type header should be explicitly set, but if not set, the most likely type
will be set based on the first non-whitespace character.

timeout.description:
Maximum time in seconds to wait for a response. The value is applied in whole seconds.
Default is `5`. A value of `0` uses the default, and values above `30` are capped at 30 seconds.

connect_timeout.description:
Maximum time in seconds to wait for a connection. The value is applied in whole seconds.
Default is `5`. A value of `0` uses the default, and values above `30` are capped at 30 seconds.

save_variables.description:
Store parsed JSON response as variables.
Default is `false`.

request.description: Send a GET, POST, PUT, or DELETE request to a remote URL.
request.title: request

return.description:
Return a value from an execute call or exit the script.
The value can be a string, number, object, or array. Booleans and `null` can appear inside an object or array, or result from resolving a variable reference,
but are not accepted directly as the whole return value.
SWML variables and expressions are resolved before the value is stored: in a string value, and in every string inside an object or array.
Object keys are not resolved. A string that is a single variable reference keeps that variable's JSON type; a reference combined with other text produces a string.
After resolution, the value can nest objects and arrays at most 62 levels deep. A deeper value is not stored, `return_value` keeps its previous value if it had one,
and the section still ends.
return.title: return

digits.description:
The digits to send. Valid values are 0123456789*#ABCDWw; A, B, C and D can also be lowercase.
Character W is a 1 second delay, and w is a 500ms delay.
After variable expansion, the value must contain at least one valid character and at most 99 characters,
counting W and w. A longer sequence is not sent, and `send_digits_result` is still `success`.

send_digits.description:
Send digit presses as DTMF tones.
For a live inbound call that hasn't been answered yet, the method first attempts to answer it.
send_digits.title: send_digits

document.description: URL to the PDF document to fax.

header_info.description:
Header text to include on the fax.
When omitted or empty, the call's destination address is used (the destination number for phone calls).

identity.description:
Station identity to report.
When omitted, the call's originating address is used (the calling number for phone calls).

status_url.description: http or https URL to deliver send_fax status events

send_fax.description:
Send a fax.
For a live inbound call that hasn't been answered yet, the method first attempts to answer it.
send_fax.title: send_fax

send_sms.description: Send an outbound SMS or MMS message to a PSTN phone number.
send_sms.title: send_sms

set.description:
Set script variables to the specified values.
Accepts an object mapping variable names to values. Each name must be an ASCII letter or underscore followed by up to 255 ASCII letters,
digits, or underscores, optionally prefixed with `vars.`; `vars.foo` sets the same variable as `foo`.
These naming rules apply only to the variable names, not to keys inside an assigned object.
Values can be any JSON value. After variable expansion, each value can nest objects and arrays at most 62 levels deep; a deeper value is not stored.
Variables set using set can be removed using unset.
set.title: set

duration.description:
The amount of time to sleep in milliseconds.
Must be a positive integer. Can also be set to `-1` for the sleep to never end.

sleep.description: Pause execution for a specified duration.
sleep.title: sleep

sip_refer.description:
Send SIP REFER to a SIP call.
Set the target with `to_uri` or its alias `to`; at least one is required.
sip_refer.title: sip_refer

stop_denoise.description: Stop noise reduction that was started with denoise.
stop_denoise.title: stop_denoise

control_id.description:
Identifier for the recording to stop.
If not set, the last recording started will be stopped.

ID of the stream to stop.
If not set, it will stop the most recent stream started.

ID of the tap to stop.
If not set, it will shut off the most recent tap session.

url.description: Secure WebSocket URI (wss://) to stream the call audio to.

control_id.description: Identifier for this stream to use with `stop_stream`. If not set, one is generated and stored in the `stream_control_id` variable.

track.description:
Audio track to stream:
    `inbound_track` for what the caller says,
    `outbound_track` for what the caller hears,
    `both_tracks` for both.
    Default is `"inbound_track"`.
    Accepts a SWML variable reference that resolves to one of these values.

codec.description:
Codec to use for the streamed audio. Freeform and endpoint-specific.
Common values include `PCMU`, `PCMA`, and `OPUS`.

status_url.description:
HTTP or HTTPS URL to deliver stream status events.
Accepts a SWML variable reference that resolves to an HTTP or HTTPS URL.

status_url_method.description:
Has no effect on stream status callbacks: SignalWire always sends `calling.call.stream` events to `status_url` with POST, whatever this is set to, so you can leave it unset.
Possible Values: [`GET`, `POST`]. Default is `"POST"`.
Accepts a SWML variable reference that resolves to one of these values.

authorization_bearer_token.description: Bearer token sent as an `Authorization` header during the WebSocket handshake.

custom_parameters.description: Custom key-value pairs sent to the WebSocket endpoint in the start message.

stream.description:
Start a background audio stream from the call to a WebSocket endpoint. Runs alongside the call as an independent operation.
For an inbound call that has not been answered and is not ending, the method attempts to answer it before starting the stream.
stream.title: stream

variable.description:
Name of the variable whose value needs to be compared.
The value is converted to a string before it is looked up in `case`: strings are used as is, booleans become `true` or `false`,
and numbers and other JSON values use their compact JSON text, so a value of `5` matches the key `"5"`.
A SWML variable reference in `variable` must resolve to a variable name.

case.description:
Object of key-mapped values to array of SWML methods to execute.
Each key is a value to match, and its array of SWML methods runs when the variable's value matches the key.
When no key matches and there is no `default`, no branch runs, a warning is reported, and execution continues with the next method while the call is still active.

default.description: Array of SWML methods to execute if no cases match.

switch.description: Execute different instructions based on a variable's value.
switch.title: switch

uri.description:
Destination of the tap media stream: `rtp://IP:port`, `ws://example.com`, or `wss://example.com`.
For RTP, the address must be a public IPv4 address followed by a port; hostnames, private addresses, and IPv6 addresses are not accepted.

control_id.description:
Identifier for this tap to use with `stop_tap`.
If not set, one is generated and stored in the `tap_control_id` variable.

direction.description:
Direction of the audio to tap:
    `speak` for what party says,
    `listen` for what party hears,
    `both` for what party hears and says.
    Default is `"speak"`.
    Accepts a SWML variable reference that resolves to one of these values.

codec.description:
Codec to use for the tap media stream.
Possible Values: [`PCMU`, `PCMA`]
Default is `"PCMU"`.
Accepts a SWML variable reference that resolves to one of these values.

rtp_ptime.description:
If `uri` is a `rtp://` this will set the packetization time of the media in milliseconds.
Must be a multiple of 10 from `10` to `120`. A number outside this range is rejected even when `uri` is a WebSocket URI, where `rtp_ptime` otherwise has no effect.
Default is `20` milliseconds.

status_url.description: http or https URL to deliver tap status events

tap.description:
Start background call tap. Media is streamed over Websocket or RTP to customer controlled URI.
For an inbound call that has not been answered and is not ending, the method attempts to answer it before starting the tap.
tap.title: tap

status_url.description:
An HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives status callbacks for this transcription:
recording events (`calling.call.transcribe`) when recording starts and finishes,
the transcript result (`calling.transcript.completed` or `calling.transcript.failed`),
and possibly `calling.error` if the transcription fails to start.
Accepts a SWML variable reference that resolves to an HTTP or HTTPS URL.

transcribe.description:
Record the call in the background and transcribe the recording after it stops.
Recording starts when this instruction runs, so audio from earlier in the call is not included, and continues until it is stopped with `transcribe_stop` or the call ends.
Execution continues to the next instruction while the call proceeds.
Transcription runs after recording stops and completes asynchronously, so the transcript can arrive some time after the call ends.
The recording is transcribed as U.S. English (`en-US`); there is no option to choose another language.
For real-time transcription delivered as the call happens, use `live_transcribe` instead.
Only one transcription can be active on a call at a time.
transcribe.title: transcribe

transcribe_stop.description:
Stop the transcription currently running on the call, started with `transcribe`.
No parameters are required.
transcribe_stop.title: transcribe_stop

dest.description:
Specifies where to transfer to. The value can be one of:
- <section_name> - section in the SWML document to jump to
- A URL (http or https) - URL to fetch next document from. Sends HTTP POST.
  Authentication can also be set in the URL in the format of username:password@url.

Relay application destinations (`relay:`) are not supported.
The value must not be empty, including after variable expansion. A value that expands
to an empty string stops execution with an error.

params.description:
Named parameters to send to transfer destination.
Accepts an object mapping variable names to values.
After variable expansion, the value can nest at most 63 levels of objects and arrays
on any branch, counting `params` itself; objects and arrays share the same limit.
Deeper nesting stops the transfer with an error.
Default is not set.

meta.description:
User data, ignored by SignalWire.
Accepts an object mapping variable names to values.
Default is not set.

transfer.description:
Transfer the execution of the script to a different SWML section or URL.
Once the transfer is complete, the script will continue executing SWML from the new location.
transfer.title: transfer

unset.description:
Unset specified variables. The variables may have been set using the set method
or as a byproduct of other statements or methods.
Accepts a single variable name as a string or an array of variable names.
Each name is a literal variable name, not a variable reference: an ASCII letter or underscore followed by up to 255 ASCII letters,
digits, or underscores, optionally prefixed with `vars.`.
`unset` removes top-level variables of the current call; `foo` and `vars.foo` remove the same variable, and the whole value is removed.
Dotted child paths and other namespaces such as `call` or `params` cannot be unset.
unset.title: unset

payment_connector_url.description:
The URL to make POST requests with all the gathered payment details. Must be an HTTPS URL,
or a SWML variable that resolves to one.
This URL is used to process the final payment transaction and return the results through the response.

Visit [pay documentation](/docs/swml/reference/calling/pay#payment_connector_url) for more important information.

charge_amount.description: The amount to charge against payment method passed in the request. `Float` value with no currency prefix passed as string. When omitted, `0.00` is sent to your payment connector.

currency.description: Uses the ISO 4217 currency code of the charge amount.

description.description: Custom description of the payment provided in the request.

input.description: The method of how to collect the payment details. Currently only `dtmf` mode is supported.

language.description: Language to use for prompts being played to the caller by the `pay` method.

max_attempts.description:
Number of attempts the caller gets to enter each payment detail, such as the card number or expiration date.
Each detail is counted separately. Set a value from `1` to `3`.
Values outside that range are ignored, and the default `1` is used instead.
With the default `1`, the caller gets no retry after a failed entry.

min_postal_code_length.description: The minimum length of the postal code the user must enter.

parameters.description: Array of parameter objects to pass to your payment processor. The parameters are user-defined key-value pairs.

payment_method.description:
The payment method to collect from the caller.

Allowed values:
- `credit-card`: collect a card number, expiration date, and (by default) security code and postal code.
- `ach-debit`: collect a bank routing number and bank account number.

Whether your payment processor accepts a given method is up to your payment connector.

bank_account_type.description:
The bank account type sent to your payment connector. Applies when `payment_method` is `ach-debit`.

Allowed values:
- `consumer-checking`
- `consumer-savings`
- `commercial-checking`

postal_code.description:
Whether to prompt for the postal code, or the postal code itself. Applies to card payments.
Pass a quoted string: an unquoted YAML or JSON boolean is rejected.
The values that turn `security_code` on, such as `"true"`, prompt the caller.

prompts.description: Array of prompt objects for customizing the audio prompts during different stages of the payment process.

say_voice.description: Alternative name for `voice`. Used only when `voice` is not set.

security_code.description:
Whether to prompt for the card security code. Applies to card payments.
Pass a quoted string: an unquoted YAML or JSON boolean is rejected.
`"true"`, `"t"`, `"yes"`, `"on"`, `"enabled"`, `"active"` and `"allow"` (in any case) and non-zero whole numbers, such as `"1"`,

status_url.description:
The URL to send requests for each status change during the payment process.

Visit [pay documentation](/docs/swml/reference/calling/pay#status_url-request-body) for more important information.

timeout.description:
Limit in seconds that pay method waits for the caller to press another digit before moving on to validate the digits captured.
Values below `3` are ignored, and the default `5` is used instead.

token_type.description:
Whether the payment is a one off payment or re-occurring.

Allowed values:
- `one-time`
- `reusable`

valid_card_types.description:
List of payment cards allowed to use in the requested payment process separated by space.

Allowed values:
- `visa`
- `mastercard`
- `amex`
- `maestro`
- `discover`
- `jcb`
- `diners-club`

voice.description:
Text-to-speech voice to use. Please refer to [TTS documentation](/docs/platform/voice/tts) for more information.
When `voice` is not set, `say_voice` is used. When neither is set, the `say_voice` SWML variable is used
if it is set; otherwise the voice is `woman`.

pay.description:
Enables secure payment processing during voice calls. When implemented, it manages the entire payment flow
including data collection, validation, and processing through your configured payment gateway.

detect_message_end.description:
Whether to keep detecting after the call is classified as a machine. If `false`, detection can finish
as soon as a machine is detected. If `true`, detection continues until a beep or the end of the
voicemail greeting is detected, or until `timeout`. A detected beep ends detection either way.
Default `false`.

detectors.description: Comma-separated string of detectors to enable. Valid values: `amd`, `fax`.

end_silence_timeout.description: How long to wait for voice to finish, in seconds. Default `1.0`. Must be at least `1`.

initial_timeout.description: How long to wait for initial voice before giving up, in seconds. Default `4.5`. Must be at least `1`.

machine_ready_timeout.description: How long to wait for voice to finish before firing READY event, in seconds. Default is `end_silence_timeout`. Must be at least `1`.

machine_voice_threshold.description: The number of seconds of ongoing voice activity required to classify as MACHINE. Default `1.25`. Must be at least `1`.

machine_words_threshold.description: The minimum number of words that must be detected in a single utterance before classifying the call as MACHINE. Default `6`. Must be at least `1`.

status_url.description: The http(s) URL to deliver detector events to.

timeout.description: The max time to run detector. Default `30.0` seconds.

tone.description: The tone to detect, will only receive remote side tone. Default `CED`.

wait.description:
If false, the detector will run asynchronously and status_url must be set.
If true, the detector will wait for detection to complete before moving to the next SWML instruction.
Default is `true`.

detect_machine.description:
A detection method that combines AMD (Answering Machine Detection) and fax detection.
Detect whether the user on the other end of the call is a machine (fax, voicemail, etc.) or a human.
The detection result(s) will be sent to the specified status_url as a POST request
and will also be saved in the detect_result variable.

event.description:
The payload of one custom event. The object can contain any JSON values; to send several events, use several `user_event` methods.
Instead of an object, you can pass a SWML variable reference that resolves to an event object.
Variable references in the payload's string values, including strings inside nested objects and arrays, are expanded before the event is sent.
Object keys aren't expanded.
SignalWire adds call details such as `call_id`, `node_id`, and `segment_id` at the top level of the payload, so top-level fields
aren't guaranteed to arrive unchanged. Put custom data under your own key to avoid name collisions.

user_event.description:
Allows the user to set and send events to the connected client on the call.
This is useful for triggering actions on the client side.
Commonly used with the [browser-sdk](/docs/browser-sdk/v3/js/reference/signalwire/client).
Each `user_event` method sends one `user_event` event, whose payload is the `event` object.
On an unanswered inbound call, this method first attempts to answer the call before sending the event.

SWMLVar.description:
A SWML variable reference for dynamic value substitution at runtime.

Use the `${varname}` or `%{varname}` syntax to reference variables that will be resolved when the SWML is executed.
Variables can be:
- **SignalWire-provided variables**: System variables like `${call.from}`, `${call.to}`, `${call.direction}`, etc.
- **User-defined variables**: Custom variables set via `set_global_data` action or passed in the initial SWML script's `global_data` object.
- **Function return values**: Variables populated from SWAIG function responses.

Example: `${global_data.customer_name}` will be replaced with the value of `customer_name` from the global_data object at runtime.

global_data.description:
A key-value object for storing data that persists throughout the AI session.
Can be set initially in the SWML script or modified during the conversation using the set_global_data action.
The global_data object is accessible everywhere in the AI session: prompts, AI parameters,
and SWML returned from SWAIG functions. Access properties using template strings (e.g. ${global_data.property_name}).

hints.description:
Words and phrases that help the agent understand what the caller says. Each string is passed to speech
recognition as a hint, making that word or phrase more likely to be recognized.
Hints don't change how the agent speaks; use `pronounce` for that.
An object can set a `hint`, a `pattern` and `replace` pair that rewrites matching text in what the agent
hears before the AI reads it, or both.

languages.description:
An array of JSON objects defining supported languages in the conversation.
Mutually exclusive with `multilingual`: if both are set, `multilingual` is used and
this array is ignored.

multilingual.description:
Configures a single agent to detect the caller's language and answer in it, switching
as the caller switches. Use this instead of `languages` when one conversation may span
several languages. Mutually exclusive with `languages`: if both are set, `multilingual`
is used and `languages` is ignored.

params.description: A JSON object containing parameters as key-value pairs.

post_prompt.description: The final set of instructions and configuration settings to send to the agent.

post_prompt_url.description: The URL to which to send status callbacks and reports. Authentication can also be set in the url in the format of `username:password@url`.

post_prompt_auth_user.description: The username for basic authentication on `post_prompt_url`. A username embedded in the URL takes precedence.

post_prompt_auth_password.description: The password for basic authentication on `post_prompt_url`. A password embedded in the URL takes precedence.

pronounce.description: An array of JSON objects to clarify the AI's pronunciation of words or expressions.

prompt.description:
Defines the AI agent's personality, goals, behaviors, and instructions for handling conversations.
The prompt establishes how the agent should interact with callers, what information it should gather,
and how it should respond to various scenarios. It is recommended to write prompts using markdown formatting.

SWAIG.description: An object that configures the functions the agent can call during the dialogue: user-defined `functions`, shared `defaults`, `includes`, `native_functions`, `mcp_servers`, and `internal_fillers`.

voice.description:
The voice the agent speaks with when neither `languages` nor `multilingual` is set.
String format: `<engine id>.<voice id>`, with an optional `:<model id>` suffix for engines that offer a
choice of model, the same format as `languages[].voice`. When `languages` or `multilingual` is set, the
voices configured there are used instead.

agent.description:
The ID of an AI agent saved in your SignalWire Space, such as the `agent_id` of an AI agent
created with the REST API. The agent runs with its saved configuration. Other settings placed next
to `agent` are ignored, so set `agent` on its own.
Don't combine `agent` with `prompt`: if both are present, the inline configuration runs and `agent`
is ignored.

prompt.description:
The operator prompt that instructs the sidecar how to coach the agent. May be a plain string or a Prompt Object Model (POM).
SignalWire automatically adds built-in instructions for the sidecar's role, so your prompt only needs to describe the coaching behavior. When omitted, the sidecar uses a minimal default prompt, so setting one is strongly recommended.

lang.description:
The conversation language as a single BCP-47 tag. Sets the speech recognition language and is shared with the model as a hint.
Required to start a sidecar; a summarize request (`action.summarize`) can omit it.

model.description: The model used for the sidecar's advice and its end-of-call summaries. Suggested values: `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `gpt-4.1-nano`. **Default:** `gpt-4o-mini`.

direction.description: The call legs to observe. Both legs are required, in either order — an empty or single-leg value is rejected. When omitted, both legs are observed. **Default:** both legs (`remote-caller` and `local-caller`).

customer_role.description: Which leg is the customer, used as the turn-end trigger source. **Default:** `remote-caller`.

url.description:
The webhook URL the sidecar POSTs its callbacks to. Receives both transcription events and sidecar callbacks.
When unset, callbacks are published only on the relay topic and no webhook POST is made.
Basic auth can be embedded in the URL in the format `username:password@url`.

SWAIG.description: SWAIG functions and MCP servers available to the sidecar.

permissions.description: SWAIG permission overrides. Defaults to all permissions enabled.

global_data.description:
A key-value object of data that is available throughout the sidecar session. You can reference it in the prompt with variable expansion, and it is included in the requests sent to your tools.
It also persists across sessions on the same call leg.

hints.description: Hints that improve speech recognition of specific terms, such as product names, competitor names, jargon, or customer names. Strongly recommended.

action.description:
Summarize the conversation instead of starting a sidecar. When you include `action.summarize`,
the request asks the sidecar already attached to the call for a one-off summary and returns
rather than attaching a sidecar. The other properties, including `lang`, are not used and can be omitted.

AISidecarSummarizeRequest.description: Asks the sidecar already attached to the call for a one-off summary of the conversation.
AISidecarSummarizeRequest.title: AISidecarSummarizeRequest object

global_data.description:
Initial data shared by all of the agent's SWAIG functions. It is sent with every function call to your
`web_hook_url`, is available to `data_map` templates under `session_data.global_data`, and is included in the
post-prompt summary report. The `set_global_data` and `unset_global_data` actions change it during the call.

params.description: A JSON object containing parameters as key-value pairs.

post_prompt.description:
Optional instructions for the summary written when the conversation ends, as `text` or `pom`.
When omitted, a default summary instruction is used. Has no effect unless `post_prompt_url` is set.

post_prompt_url.description:
The URL that receives the conversation summary report when the conversation ends. The summary is written
only when this is set. Authentication can also be set in the url in the format of `username:password@url`.

prompt.description: Establishes the initial set of instructions and settings to configure the agent.

SWAIG.description: An object containing the user-defined `functions` the agent can call during the dialogue and their `defaults`.

else.description: Sequence of SWML methods to execute when none of the other conditions evaluate to true.

from_name.description:
The caller ID name shown to the person you're calling, displayed alongside the `from` number
(sometimes called CNAM).
Applies to SIP calls only — it has no effect on calls to phone numbers.
When set at the top level, every destination in a `serial`, `parallel`, or `serial_parallel`
group uses this name, unless that destination sets its own `from_name`.
Use 1 to 70 characters after variable expansion: letters, digits, spaces, and `_`, `.`, `-`, `+`, or `,`.
Text and variables can be combined, such as `Support ${vars.dept}`.

headers.description:
Custom SIP headers to add to INVITE. It has no effect on calls to phone numbers.
In `serial`, `parallel`, and `serial_parallel`, every SIP destination uses these headers
unless it sets its own `headers`.

codecs.description:
Codecs to offer, as a comma-separated string (`"PCMU,PCMA"`) or an array of strings (`["PCMU", "PCMA"]`).
Supported codecs are `PCMU`, `PCMA`, `OPUS`, `G722`, `G729`, `AMR-WB`, `VP8`, and `H264`.
It has no effect on calls to phone numbers.
In `serial`, `parallel`, and `serial_parallel`, every SIP destination uses these codecs
unless it sets its own `codecs`.
Based on SignalWire settings.

webrtc_media.description:
If true, WebRTC media is offered to the SIP endpoint.
It has no effect on calls to phone numbers.
In `serial`, `parallel`, and `serial_parallel`, every SIP destination uses this value
unless it sets its own `webrtc_media`.
Default is `false`.

session_timeout.description:
Time, in seconds, to set the SIP `Session-Expires` header in INVITE.
Must be a positive, non-zero number. Values from 1 to 15000 take effect; a larger value is
accepted but ignored, so the default `Session-Expires` value is used.
It has no effect on calls to phone numbers.
Applies only when dialing a single SIP destination with `to`. In `serial`, `parallel`, and
`serial_parallel`, the top-level value has no effect: set `session_timeout` on each SIP destination instead.
Based on SignalWire settings.

ringback.description:
Ringback to play to the caller while phone, SIP, and Resource Address destinations ring. Can be:
- A `play` URI, or an array of `play` URIs, to play as the ringback tone
- `false` to turn off SignalWire's ringback tone and pass the destination's early media
  (for example, its own ringback or announcements) through to the caller
- `true` to keep the default ringback tone
If not specified, SignalWire plays a standard ringback tone.

anyOf.description:
Execute a sequence of instructions depending on the value of a JavaScript condition.
Conditions are checked in array order. The first condition whose `when` evaluates to true runs its `then` instructions,
and the remaining conditions are skipped. The `else` entry runs only when no condition evaluates to true.
At most one `else` entry is allowed, and it doesn't have to be the last entry.
When no condition matches and there is no `else` entry, execution continues with the next method after `cond`.
anyOf.title: cond

result.description:
Action to take based on the result of the call. This will run once the peer leg of the call has ended.
Will use the switch method when the return_value is an object, and will use the cond method when the return_value is an array.

timeout.description:
Time, in seconds, to wait for the call to be answered.
Default is 60 seconds.

max_duration.description:
Maximum duration, in seconds, allowed for the call.
Default is `14400` seconds.

answer_on_bridge.description:
Delay answer until the B-leg answers.
Default is `false`.

confirm.description:
Confirmation to execute when the call is connected. Can be either:
- A URL (string) that returns a SWML document
- An array of SWML methods to execute inline. Only these methods are allowed, including inside
  `cond` and `switch` branches: `cond`, `switch`, `set`, `unset`, `hangup`, `play`, `prompt`,
  `record`, `record_call`, `stop_record_call`, `tap`, `stop_tap`, `stream`, `stop_stream`,
  `transcribe`, `transcribe_stop`, `send_digits`, `send_sms`, `denoise`, `stop_denoise`, and `user_event`.

confirm_timeout.description:
Time, in seconds, allowed for the `confirm` SWML to run on the answered destination, whether it is
fetched from a URL or given inline. When not set, the destination's `timeout` is used.

call_state_url.description:
Webhook URL to send call status change notifications to. Authentication can also be set in the URL in the format of `username:password@url`.
Applies only to phone, SIP, and Resource Address destinations. A destination whose `to` starts with
`queue:`, `call:`, or `stream:` can't have `call_state_url` or `call_state_events`, and a top-level value doesn't apply to
those destinations. Queue lifecycle events go to the `status_url` set on `enter_queue`; stream events
go to the stream's `status_url`.

execute_after_queue.description:
SWML to execute on this call after its bridge with the queued call ends. Only applies when
`to` starts with `queue:`. When omitted, the call hangs up when the bridge ends. Either way,
the script does not continue past `connect` once a queued call has been bridged.
If no queued call is bridged (for example, the queue is empty or doesn't exist), `connect` fails,
`connect_result` is set to `failed`, and `result` runs.
Can be either:
- A URL (http or https) that returns a SWML document
- An inline SWML document (as a JSON string)

call_state_events.description:
An array of call state event names to be notified about.
Allowed event names are:
    - `created`
    - `ringing`
    - `answered`
    - `ended`
Each array item can also be a SWML variable reference that resolves to one of these names.

stop_all_on_reject.description:
Stop ringing and disconnect the caller when a destination rejects the call. Can be either:
- `true` to stop when a destination is busy or declines the call
- A non-empty array of the reasons to stop on: `busy`, `decline`, `noAnswer`
When a destination rejects the call with a matching reason, the destinations ringing alongside it
stop ringing. If `connect` then fails with that reason, the `result` block runs first, and then
the caller is disconnected.

status_url.description:
HTTP or HTTPS URL to deliver connect status events.
These events report the overall status of the connect operation
(connecting, connected, failed, disconnected) via a `calling.call.connect` event.
When `to` is a single `stream:` destination, this URL receives the stream status notifications instead,
and it can still use `http://` or `https://`.

to.description:
Destination to dial. Can be:
- Phone number in E.164 format, including the leading `+` (e.g., "+15552345678")
- SIP URI, with a `sip:` or `sips:` prefix (e.g., "sip:alice@example.com")
- Resource Address (e.g., "/public/test_room")
- Queue (e.g., "queue:support")
- Call in progress in the same project, by call ID (e.g., "call:ba79c846-4834-42b9-9cd3-2f87c30f2972")
- WebSocket stream, using `wss://` (e.g., "stream:wss://example.com/audio")
The `queue:`, `call:`, and `stream:` prefixes are case-sensitive and must be lowercase.

username.description: SIP username to use for authentication when dialing a SIP URI. Has no effect on calls to phone numbers.

password.description: SIP password to use for authentication when dialing a SIP URI. Has no effect on calls to phone numbers.

name.description: Stream name identifier. Only applies to stream destinations.

codec.description:

Codec can include rate and ptime modifiers (e.g., `PCMU@40i`, `L16@24000h@40i`).
Only applies to stream destinations.

realtime.description:
Enable realtime mode for bidirectional audio.
Only applies to stream destinations.

status_url_method.description:
HTTP method for the stream status webhook.
Only applies to stream destinations.

authorization_bearer_token.description: Bearer token sent as an `Authorization` header during the WebSocket handshake. Only applies to stream destinations.

custom_parameters.description: Custom key-value pairs sent in the WebSocket start message. Only applies to stream destinations.

muted.description: Whether to join the conference in a muted state. If set to `true`, the participant will be muted upon joining. Default `false`.

beep.description: Sets the behavior of the beep sound when joining or leaving the conference. Default `"true"`.

start_on_enter.description:
Whether this participant can start the conference. A conference starts once at least one participant
with `start_on_enter` set to `true` has joined and the number of participants has reached
`min_participants` (2 by default). Until then, participants wait. Default `true`.

end_on_exit.description: Ends the conference when the main participant leaves. This means the end action will not wait on more participants to leave before ending. Default `false`.

wait_url.description:
A URL that SignalWire requests with an HTTP `GET` while this participant waits for the conference to start.
Default hold music is played if not set. Set it to an empty string (`""`) to play silence instead.

max_participants.description: The maximum number of participants allowed in the conference. If the limit is reached, new participants will not be able to join. Maximum `250`. Default `250`.

min_participants.description:
The number of participants that must join before the conference starts. Set it to `1` to let a single
participant with `start_on_enter` start the conference. Use a value from 1 up to `max_participants`.
When both are set, a `min_participants` larger than `max_participants` is rejected. An invalid number written
directly in the document makes the document invalid, so it doesn't run. An invalid value that comes from a
variable, such as `0` or a number larger than `max_participants`, makes the join fail and sets
`join_conference_result` to `failed`.
Like `max_participants`, it is set when the conference is created; joining an existing conference doesn't change it.
Default `2`.

record.description:
Enables or disables recording of the conference. Default `"do-not-record"`.
With `record-from-start`, recording starts once at least two participants have joined, even if
`min_participants` lets the conference start earlier. Recording is configured when the conference is created.

region.description: Specifies the geographical region requested for hosting the conference. Default `"global"`.

trim.description: If set to `trim-silence`, it will remove silence from the start of the recording. If set to `do-not-trim`, it will keep the silence. Default `"trim-silence"`.

coach.description:

The coach hears the whole conference, but is heard only by the coached participant; the other participants cannot hear the coach.
The call SID must belong to a call that is currently connected to the in-progress conference. Specifying a call SID that does not exist or is no longer connected will result in a failure.

status_callback_method.description:

Notifications in the `relay` format (see `status_callback_event_type`) are always sent with `POST`, even if `GET` is set.

The stream is set up only while the conference has not started yet; a `stream` sent by a participant
